blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, cash and accrual are not competing methods — they are two different lenses that together tell the real story of a company. Accrual shows whether the business is economically performing; cash shows whether the business is financially surviving. A thoughtful senior finance team presents both at every major review, because each asks a different question and each warns about a different kind of trouble.

Accrual can flatter a business that is growing receivables faster than its customers can sustain. Cash can punish a business that has made long-term investments which will pay off later. The combination catches what either number alone cannot.

Executives who insist on seeing both — and who understand the gap between them — rarely find themselves surprised by the finances. Those who look at only one tend to be surprised twice a year, every year, and usually at the worst possible moment.

items.q: According to the text, what is the relationship between cash and accrual at senior level?
options: They are two lenses that together tell the real story
Accrual is reliable and cash is not
They are competing methods that must be reconciled
Only cash matters once a company matures
items.why: "they are two different lenses that together tell the real story of a company."

items.q: Which question does the accrual view answer?
options: Whether the business is economically performing
Whether the business is financially surviving
Whether receivables are collectable
Whether investments will pay off
items.why: "Accrual shows whether the business is economically performing."

items.q: Why can accrual 'flatter' a business?
options: It always overstates the value of assets
It can show growth in receivables customers may not be able to sustain
It reports profit only in cash terms
It hides long-term investments from the board
items.why: "Accrual can flatter a business that is growing receivables faster than its customers can sustain."

items.q: The text suggests that the author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: One well-chosen number is enough for a senior review
Each view warns about a different kind of trouble
The gap between the two views can be informative
Cash can understate a company that is investing for the future
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que quem olha só um número acaba surpreendido — logo um número só não basta.

items.q: What does the closing line about being 'surprised twice a year… at the worst possible moment' imply?
options: Relying on a single view leaves you blind to a predictable risk
Executives dislike detailed finance reports
Financial surprises are unavoidable in any business
Board reviews should happen more than twice a year
items.why: Inferência: a surpresa recorrente é o preço de ignorar a outra lente — um risco que era previsível.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando o novo relatório ao board. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so what you're looking at is a single page with two columns. The left is the accrual view, the right is the cash view, and the whole point is that they sit side by side. Every month I'll add one short paragraph underneath, explaining why the two agree — or, more usefully, why they don't.

Let me show you this quarter. On accrual, we look healthy: revenue is up, margins are holding. On cash, we're tighter than the board might expect. That gap isn't an error. It's being driven by two things — a large receivable from a client who's paying slowly, and the plant upgrade we signed off last year, which won't earn its keep until next summer.

Here's what I'd ask you to take away. Neither number is the truth on its own. If we'd only been shown the accrual page, we'd have felt comfortable and missed the collection risk. If we'd only been shown cash, we'd have panicked about an investment that is entirely deliberate. The paragraph in the middle is where the real conversation happens — and it's the part I'd like us to read first, before we argue about either column.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How is Sophie's board report laid out?
options: As a cash statement with accrual in an appendix
As two separate documents circulated in advance
As a chart with no written commentary
As a single page with accrual and cash side by side
items.why: "a single page with two columns… they sit side by side."

items.q: What does Sophie say drives the gap between the two views this quarter?
options: A slow-paying receivable and the plant upgrade signed off last year
A change in the reporting standard
A sudden fall in revenue and margins
An accounting error in the receivables ledger
items.why: "a large receivable from a client who's paying slowly, and the plant upgrade we signed off last year."

items.q: According to Sophie, what would have happened if the board had seen only the accrual page?
options: They would have panicked about the investment
They would have felt comfortable and missed the collection risk
They would have cancelled the plant upgrade
They would have questioned the margins
items.why: "we'd have felt comfortable and missed the collection risk."

items.q: When Sophie says the gap 'isn't an error', she is implying that…
options: accrual should be abandoned in favour of cash
the difference itself carries meaningful information
the cash column was calculated incorrectly
the two views should always be reconciled to zero
items.why: Inferência: para Sophie a lacuna é sinal, não falha — é onde está a informação relevante.

items.q: Why does Sophie want the board to read the middle paragraph first?
options: Because the columns are only estimates
Because it summarises the numbers so the columns can be skipped
Because it frames the two columns so the discussion starts from the right question
Because the board dislikes reading figures
items.why: Inferência: o parágrafo do meio explica por que as visões divergem, orientando a conversa antes da disputa sobre cada coluna.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Cash and accrual are two lenses, not two methods." Here a lens is…
options: a piece of reporting software
a way of viewing the same reality
a strict accounting rule
a regulatory requirement
items.why: Lens = lente: uma perspectiva sobre a mesma realidade, não um método rival.

items.q: "Strong margins made the quarter look better than it was; the receivables were quietly flattering the numbers." To flatter here means to…
options: reconcile two figures
make something look better than it really is
delay a payment
audit an account
items.why: To flatter = favorecer, fazer parecer melhor do que é.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The plant upgrade is a ___ investment; it won't earn its keep until next summer."
options: over-the-counter
short-term
long-term
written-off
items.why: Long-term investment = investimento de longo prazo, que só retorna mais adiante.

items.q: "The interesting figure is often the gap between the two views." The gap is…
options: the average of the two figures
the error margin of the audit
the difference between them
the total of both columns
items.why: Gap = lacuna: a diferença entre as duas leituras, muitas vezes o número que importa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Revenue is growing faster than our customers can ___ their payments."
options: sustain
flatter
punish
perform
items.why: To sustain = sustentar: manter os pagamentos ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de finanças e reporte. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board signed off on the plant upgrade last year." To sign off on means to…
options: postpone indefinitely
formally approve
comment informally
audit
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "The upgrade won't earn its keep until next summer." This means it will not…
options: justify its cost through the value it produces
require any further spending
be depreciated on schedule
appear on the balance sheet
items.why: Earn its keep = compensar o custo, valer o que se gastou.

items.q: "If we only look at cash, we lose sight of whether the business is truly performing." To lose sight of means to…
options: stop paying attention to
report to the regulator
double-check carefully
deliberately hide
items.why: Lose sight of = perder de vista, deixar de considerar algo importante.

items.q: "Presenting both views helps us get ahead of the collection risk." To get ahead of a risk means to…
options: report it after it occurs
underestimate it deliberately
pass it to another department
deal with it before it becomes a problem
items.why: Get ahead of = antecipar-se a algo, agir antes que vire problema.

items.q: "A single view can paper over a serious cash shortfall." To paper over means to…
options: highlight in a report
conceal a problem without fixing it
resolve permanently
escalate to the board
items.why: Paper over = encobrir superficialmente um problema, sem de fato resolvê-lo.
